newsitem.title: USA: PG&E to sell distribution lines to Modesto.
newsitem.headline: PG&E to sell distribution lines to Modesto.

text.p: PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas & Electric Co announced Thursday plans to sell its electric distribution system in four San Joaquin Valley cities to the Modesto Irrigation District as part of a settlement agreement.

PG&E said the $110 million sale includes five substations, 800 miles of power lines and associated equipment that serves 30,000 customers in the cities of Ripon, Escalon, Riverbank and Oakdale and adjacent unincorporated areas.

The agreement also establishes new boundaries for each utility's service territory, settles litigation between the Modesto utility and PG&E, and resolves responsibility for charges associated with state legislation requiring deregulation of California's electric industry.
The sale is proposed to become effective January 1, 1998, pending the approval of local, state and federal government regulatory agencies.

PG&E noted the company's distribution facilities are generally not for sale, but the Modesto deal resulted from a dispute over plans by the public utility to sell power to a PG&E customer last year before state law on the practice was in place.
